sites.title: Sites

sites.saved_reload: Config saved. Click Reload to apply.

settings.title: Settings
settings.bind_title: Bind a domain to the panel
settings.bind_desc: Add a domain that reverse-proxies to port {{port}} on this host.
settings.bind_hint: Appends a reverse_proxy block to the Caddyfile and reloads the gateway. The domain must already resolve to this host.
settings.uninstall_desc: Uninstalling isn't a single click — here are the exact steps to run on the server.
settings.uninstall_warn: The last step deletes all panel data (database, trash, config). It cannot be undone.
settings.contact_desc: Reach us through either of these if you run into trouble.
settings.system_desc: How the server behaves: memory, time, network, patches.
settings.panel_desc: Things about this panel: domain, contact, uninstall.

settings.info_desc: What this panel is, whether an update is out, and how to remove it.
settings.site_title_desc: Shown in the menu bar and the browser tab. Empty keeps ZOPS.
settings.domain_current: Panel entrance: {{domain}}. It is marked on the home page and the site list, and deleting it asks separately.

settings.access_closed: Public access is off. The panel is restarting.
settings.uninstall_only_panel: This removes the panel only: stop the service, delete the binary and the zops command. Docker, Caddy, and other services stay. The data directory is kept.
settings.uninstall_confirm: The page will disconnect. This cannot be undone from the panel.

network.desc: DNS, the Docker image registries, and WireGuard.

network.registry_desc: Mirrors and insecure registries in daemon.json. Other fields are kept. Docker restarts when you save.
network.vpn_desc: WireGuard. Import a config, then start or stop the tunnel. If wg is missing, this page will not install it.

mcp.scope_write_desc: Can restart containers, deploy, edit the gateway
mcp.create_desc: Give it a name you will recognise (“Codex desktop”, “Workbuddy”), pick the scope. The token is shown once here, and kept on this browser so the card can copy it later.

mcp.config_ready: Paste this straight into the agent.
mcp.config_missing: This browser has no copy of that token (created before the update). Disconnect and create a new one to copy it.

mcp.summary: {{conns}} connections · {{active}} in use · {{calls}} agent calls in 24h

screen.title: Screen
screen.live_empty_hint: The panel tails Caddy's access log every 15s. If it stays empty, check that your sites enable an access log.
screen.server_unknown: Server location unknown — no inbound lines
screen.sec_note: Blocked = requests rejected by the gateway rules (403). Scanners/tools = script or scanner user agents. Locations come from an IP database and shift with proxies and carrier NAT — treat them as a hint.

about.title: About
about.intro: ZOPS puts one server's observation and control into a single surface: load and containers, the Caddy gateway and its sites, files and logs, scheduled tasks, and an MCP endpoint for AI agents. No cloud account — it runs on the machine it manages, and the data stays there.
about.footer: Found a bug, have an idea, or want a feature? Open an issue or just send an email.
about.check_failed: Couldn't reach the release manifest (network or CDN) — showing the last known result
about.updating: Downloading and swapping — the panel will restart itself, keep this page open
about.copy_failed: Copy failed — select the text and copy manually
about.fingerprint_hint: An agent over MCP reports this same fingerprint. Different version = it is talking to another panel; different start time = a different process. If it does not match, do not trust its data.
about.update_started: Update started: the panel replaces itself and restarts in ~30s
about.cannot_apply: This instance can't self-update (it isn't running the installer's binary); use the copied command instead.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.subtitle: Push panel events to your chat: deploys, containers going down, pressure alerts.
notify.empty_hint: Add a Feishu or DingTalk bot and the panel will push events straight into your group.
notify.name: Name
notify.secret_placeholder: Only if signing is enabled on the bot
notify.secret_hint: Only needed when the bot has signing enabled — the panel will then sign each request the way that platform expects.
notify.remove_desc: Its events will no longer reach anyone. You can re-add the webhook later, but the delivery history is gone.
notify.hint_feishu: Feishu group → Settings → Bots → Add custom bot, then copy the webhook URL.
notify.hint_dingtalk: DingTalk group → Group settings → Smart assistant → Add bot → Custom, then copy the webhook. Fill the secret in if you chose signing.
notify.hint_wecom: WeCom group → Group settings → Group bot → Add, then copy the webhook URL.
notify.hint_slack: Slack → Apps → Incoming Webhooks → Add New Webhook, pick a channel, copy the URL.
notify.hint_discord: Discord channel → Edit channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New, copy the URL.
notify.hint_telegram: Create a bot with @BotFather, then append the chat id: …/bot<token>/sendMessage?chat_id=<id>.
notify.hint_generic: POSTs {event, title, text, host} as JSON — for your own service.

deploy.title: Apps & services
deploy.subtitle: One app = its own directory on the server + artifacts + a deploy script. Three steps after creating it: upload artifacts → write the script → run. Every run is recorded, and you can see which container it is bound to.
deploy.empty: No apps yet. Create one and it gets its own directory under /opt/docker-apps/ on the server.
deploy.step1_hint: Drop files here, or click to choose (artifacts, compose, configs)
deploy.confirm_delete: Delete “{{name}}”? The directory and artifacts stay on the server.
deploy.dir_hint: Creates /opt/docker-apps/<name>/ on the server. The name is used for the directory, the container and the image.
deploy.name: Service name
deploy.template_head: # runs inside /opt/docker-apps/<name>/ (that is the working directory; this is `set -e`)
deploy.adopt_desc: Create a deploy job for this running service: upload artifacts, write the deploy script, run it — every run is recorded, and you can see which container it is bound to.
deploy.kind_backend: Backend service (publishes a host port; the gateway proxies localhost:<port>)
deploy.kind_frontend: Static frontend (no host port; the gateway proxies by container name)
deploy.port_auto: Leave empty to pick a free one (8000-9999)
deploy.spec_hint: Creating writes the house-convention skeleton: docker-compose.yml (network local, restart always, TZ=Asia/Shanghai, 50m×10 log rotation), Dockerfile, deploy.sh. Existing files are never overwritten.
deploy.step1_desc: Upload what you want to deploy (a release package, compose file, configs). Skippable when only the script changed.
deploy.step2_desc: Write the deploy script that runs inside this directory, then save it.
deploy.step3_desc: Runs the script in /opt/docker-apps/<name>/ on the server, with live output.
deploy.log_hint: Not run yet. Hit “Run deploy” in the top-right and the output shows up here live.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Who knocked on this machine, with what, and which ports it currently exposes.
security.exposed_note: Services bound to 127.0.0.1 only are not exposed, so they are not listed.
security.rules_note: Read-only for now. Editing rules is not implemented — that needs a per-distro backend and a way to avoid locking yourself out.
security.ssh_empty: No records. /var/log/secure (or auth.log) has no sshd auth lines yet, or the panel cannot read it.
security.alerts_intro: Suspicious requests picked out of the access log, grouped by IP + kind + path + hour. Last 24h: {{total}} entries from {{ips}} IPs.
security.alerts_empty: No alerts. Either traffic is clean, or the first ingest has not run yet (every 15 seconds).

tools.ops_panel_info: The panel itself: version, what this credential may do, how many tools it has.
tools.ops_system_overview: Live load: CPU, memory, swap, disk, network, load average, process count. First thing to look at.
tools.ops_container_list: All Docker containers (name, image, state, ports).
tools.ops_container_status: Whether the Docker engine is up, and its version.
tools.ops_container_stop: Stop a container — that service goes down. Ask the user first.
tools.ops_container_restart: Restart a container — brief downtime. Ask the user first.
tools.ops_container_logs: Recent container logs (100 lines by default) for crashes and errors.
tools.ops_gateway_status: Caddy gateway status (running, version, config path).
tools.ops_gateway_logs: Caddy's own log (300 lines by default). First stop for 502s and certificate failures.
tools.ops_gateway_reload: Reload the Caddy config after editing the Caddyfile; a broken config is rejected.
tools.ops_caddyfile_get: Read the current Caddyfile. Take a copy before changing anything.
tools.ops_caddyfile_put: Replace the whole Caddyfile (no auto reload). Affects every domain — confirm with the user first.
tools.ops_log_source_list: Registered application log files (with paths) for ops_log_tail.
tools.ops_log_tail: Read the tail of a log file on the server.
tools.ops_automation_task_list: Configured scheduled tasks (name, cron, last / next run).
tools.ops_automation_task_run: Run a scheduled task now — its shell command runs on the server. Destructive, confirm first.
tools.ops_member_list: Panel members, their roles and permissions.
tools.ops_port_list: Listening TCP ports on the host, what owns them, and a few free ones. Check before deploying so ports do not collide.
tools.ops_notify_channel_list: Configured notification channels (Feishu / DingTalk / WeCom / Slack …) and the events they subscribe to.
tools.ops_notify_send: Push a notification to the channels subscribed to an event (deploy finished, incident handled). Event names come from ops_notify_channel_list.
tools.ops_deploy_list: Which services are already deployed here (directory + running or not). Check before deploying to avoid name clashes.
tools.ops_deploy_plan: Deploy pre-flight: port taken, missing restart policy / log rotation / timezone / network, plaintext credentials. Read-only. Run before apply.
tools.ops_deploy_apply: Write the compose file and extra files into the deploy directory, then run docker compose up -d --build. Adds services, takes ports, writes files — confirm with the user first.
tools.ops_deploy_job_list: Deploy jobs: service name, directory, status, bound container, last result.
tools.ops_deploy_job_get: One deploy job in detail: script, uploaded artifacts, recent runs.
tools.ops_deploy_job_create: Create a deploy job: makes /opt/docker-apps/<name>/ and records it. Create first, then upload artifacts and write the script.
tools.ops_deploy_job_put_script: Write the deploy script (runs with sh -c inside /opt/docker-apps/<name>/; it behaves like set -e).
tools.ops_deploy_job_put_file: Write a text artifact into the deploy directory (config, small script, compose). For binaries use HTTP: curl -T file -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://<panel>/api/ops/deploy/job/upload?id=<name>&path=<relative path>".
tools.ops_deploy_job_run: Run the deploy script. Changes production — confirm with the user first. Poll progress with ops_deploy_job_log using the returned run_id.
tools.ops_deploy_job_log: Incrementally read a deploy run's log. Pass the previous offset to continue; finished=true means it is done.
tools.ops_app_list: Built-in apps you can deploy in one click (MySQL / PostgreSQL / Redis / MinIO): image, default ports, the environment variables to fill in (which are required, minimum password length), volumes, and whether it is already installed. Read this before inventing parameters.
tools.ops_app_plan: Build an install plan without changing anything: the rendered docker-compose.yml (passwords masked), the deploy script, the data directories, and warnings about taken ports or a missing network. Read-only — show this compose to the user before installing.
tools.ops_app_install: Deploy a built-in app in one click: write the compose and its data directories, create the deploy job, run docker compose up -d. Takes ports, writes files, starts containers — confirm with the user first and run ops_app_plan first. Returns a run_id for ops_deploy_job_log.
